reason: Internal: a design bundle only (design/evaluation/), no code. Rewritten around the question it exists to answer — how does the evaluation suite establish that Nora behaves as designed — rather than around the harness plumbing an earlier draft mistook for the subject. Measured on design/09-decision-index.md: 250 decision and rule rows, 10 cite an evals/ instrument, 196 cite a unit test only, 44 cite nothing, and five of the ten point at a corpus that drives a bare model rather than Nora. Cut to the R-* rules, which are behavioural by construction: 92 of them, 4 with an eval, 52 guarded by a test that measures wiring, 36 with nothing. So the index column AGENTS.md sends readers to answers whether the code is wired while being read as an answer about behaviour. The test layer is explicitly OUT of scope: unit, integration and e2e are solved outside this repo and want standard practice, not a bespoke convention; what has no industry answer is whether an LLM agent behaves as designed, and that is the only thing in the bundle. 01-the-runner records a measured refutation of its own first proposal — moving the integration harness into nora.testing breaks the layer contract three ways, including a reverse import — and corrects the two-builders framing: both harnesses already call the same wiring, and what diverges is the setup around it plus 13 parameters defaulting to None. No decision is taken.
